FOURTH AND DEEPEST ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-05: environment/atmosphere.js lightDepth() reused scatter()'s view-density scratch array _d, so every CPU-sampled sky radiance came out ~10^4x too dim (measured zenith 7e-6 vs physical ~0.5). The exposure controller, reading a near-black sky, climbed to its ceiling; the visible 'sky' was the blown-out cloud deck; fog and aerial-perspective colours near black produced the horizon band. This is the true root cause of the round-1 SYSTEMIC 'washed out toward white' blocker and of both of environment's round-2 majors — NOT ACES tone mapping, NOT albedo authoring. The GPU LUT was unaffected (GLSL locals), which is why sun colour was always right while sky/fog colours were wrong. Fixed with a separate scratch array; wave-3 verification then proceeded against a correctly-lit world.

Wave 3 (savannah, park) verified 2026-09-05: both modules were already fully implemented in the ZIP but had never been screenshotted, scored, or documented (STATUS said 'not-started' — stale). Screenshot-tooling note for future rounds: park's own setSpeed(1) used to push every capture into a random night hour under SwiftShader (~35 game-hours burn during the 40-frame settle at ~1 fps) — capture pages must pass &speed=0, and modules that advance the clock must respect an explicitly paused clock. Also: do not run 3+ concurrent SwiftShader renders on a 12-core machine — module imports starve and pages time out.
Egress proxy blocks Poly Haven / ambientCG / all CDNs: every asset is procedural.
Screenshot tool renders through SwiftShader (software GL); fps in shots/*.json is NOT a GPU number. Draw calls, triangles and errors are real.

SECOND ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-04: environment/index.js clamped auto-exposure at 60x, and it was hitting 5.46x at golden hour / 60x at night on ordinary, correctly-lit scenes (Math.max(0, keyDir.y) kills the key-light term well before the sky actually looks dim as the sun nears the horizon). Every material several-fold overexposed, verified by reading a baked lion albedo texture directly (correct ~0.38 linear) against near-white on screen. Lowered the ceiling to 4 (commit e3a6999); night is now dim and legible with visible stars instead of blown to white, golden hour shows correct value separation between light/dark test objects instead of clipping everything. Needs a further tuning pass against real references but is no longer broken. This, independently of the sRGB double-encode, explains why several modules' screenshots looked washed out at low sun angles even after the sRGB fix — e.g. buildings' lodge preset (tod 17.5) flat-white background buildings.

THIRD ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-04: terrain/mesh.js had `mesh.receiveShadow = false; // BENCH`, a leftover benchmarking flag that silently blocked every shadow in the game from landing on the ground, anywhere. Fixed (commit e3a6999). This was the real cause of animals' round-1 'no contact shadow' blocker — animals had already shipped a drawn contact-shadow decal as a workaround, which stays in place as a complement now that real shadows also work.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-02: core/Textures.js gpu() double-encoded sRGB (shader-side linearToSRGBv plus an sRGB-internal-format render target). Linear 0.216 was stored as byte 188 instead of 128 — every albedo ~37% too bright. This, not ACES tone mapping, was the real cause of the project-wide washed-out look; the earlier 'author darker to compensate' guidance was a workaround over a core defect and is now WRONG. Core is fixed. Modules that compensated must have that compensation REMOVED: props is currently over-dark (near-black foliage), and any darkening added to animals/terrain/roads in round 2 must be re-checked.

issues.text: FIXED and verified (tools/shots/buildings-final-lodge.png): the flat-black roof shadow is gone — this was the environment exposure clamp + terrain receiveShadow bugs, both since fixed, not a buildings issue. The ground in front of the lodge now reads as correctly lit dry grass with a real soft shadow, and the background buildings show proper thatch roofs and shaded plaster walls instead of flat white boxes. Closes the loop on a cross-cutting bug chain: animals found it, environment/terrain fixed it, buildings independently confirms the fix.

Root cause found and fixed by the builder: the showcase's 8 hand-picked site anchors landed on/near water/kopjes for every candidate on this seed (0/240 valid), so the whole complex fell back to a coordinate that was itself underwater — the actual cause of earlier 'floating on water' renders. Replaced with a full-grid scan with biome/water-table rejection and slope scoring.

Buildings-only cost measured directly via api.stats(): 34 draw calls / 131,730 triangles for 25 buildings across all 16 catalogue types — well inside the <=60/<=400k spec budget. The ~276-296 draw calls seen in full-frame screenshots is terrain+props, not buildings; earlier concern about the draw-call count was based on the wrong number.

Builder's own README, honest: occasional forced placement when local slope fails even on a good site (2/25 this seed, never on water); no LOD beyond 300m; several catalogue types (fence gate, feeder, toilets, parking) only shown at overview distance, not close-up.

buildings.good: A real thatched-roof lodge with striated makuti roofing, timber rafters, chimney, stone plinth, water tank, solar panel, correct acacia silhouettes around it, and — now that the shadow bug is fixed — a coherent, correctly lit golden-hour scene. Two real bugs found and fixed along the way (site placement, windpump rotor pivot). All 6 presets load, zero errors, lint clean, buildings' own draw-call cost is well within budget.

props.good: This is the clearest before/after in the project: round 1 was a legitimate 5.5 (washed out, wrong silhouette, visible seams). Vegetation existing at all was the single biggest blocker in the project three rounds ago; it is now a strong module.

issues.text: Verification took several attempts because the overview preset (camera distance 430m) makes a 4-5m vehicle imperceptibly small — I initially misread this as 'no vehicles rendering' and, worse, briefly misdiagnosed it as a missing kit.setBodyMatrix() call based on a flawed grep pattern ('setMatrix' is not a substring of 'setBodyMatrix') before re-checking and finding the wiring is correct. The close preset settles it cleanly: vehicles are real, positioned, and rendering. Recorded so the mistake isn't repeated.
Night preset (headlights) and sighting preset (animals interaction) not yet independently reviewed.

Overview preset's vehicle scale-at-distance is a legitimate framing concern for the module's own showcase, even though it isn't a rendering bug — worth a closer default camera or a labelled close-up inset.

traffic.good: Genuinely good: a real open safari truck with tiered bench seats, clearly visible seated passengers in varied clothing colours, ribbed canopy roof, roof rack, spare wheel, khaki body paint, and a visible ground contact shadow. World-state vehicle spawning verified directly (6 vehicles with plausible, in-bounds positions). Zero console errors, 106 draw calls at close, all modules load together cleanly.

issues.text: terrain/road/close/night presets not yet independently reviewed (overview and building both confirmed good).
Select/inspect picking is radius/nearest-based rather than a true mesh raycast — a documented, deliberate simplification given the public API contract, not a bug.

tools.good: This is the module that makes the game playable rather than watchable, and it delivers: a real tool framework (activate/deactivate/undo/redo >=50 steps), and I independently verified two presets. `overview` shows the full scripted session actually working end-to-end — a curving gravel road crossing the river with a real bridge, a large painted habitat overlay, structures placed — all through the module's own public API, no shortcuts. `building` shows a working ghost preview: the real placed lodge with a semi-transparent red overlay correctly signalling an invalid (occupied) placement. Also found and fixed a genuine bug during its own testing: an unbounded terrain-raise stroke that, under this session's heavy concurrent load, once grew tall enough to embed the camera inside solid terrain — now capped, which fixes real gameplay too. README is thorough: full API, undo/redo mechanics explained per-tool, cost model, and an honest known-gaps list.

issues.text: FIXED and verified (tools/shots/sav-kopje-fix-d.png / -e.png, 2026-09-07): the male lion is unmistakable at 8 m — dark mane, tan flank, legs grounded, a lioness standing right third and another lying left, kopje backdrop, sun behind the lens. Root cause was three stacked occluders invisible to the terrain-only LOS check: the spot sat on the kopje's steep skirt (legs swallowed by a rock lip), a tall dead shrub ~3 m off the cleared lane leaned across the subject, and a giant boulder rooted beside the lens filled half the frame; dead-centre front light also flattened the male toward the old 'pale box'. showcase.js now requires dry AND slope < 0.14 at the spot, seeds the bearing 20° off the sun for three-quarter light, marches the camera (8→30 m) requiring camera-spot slope < 0.18, and widens props.clear to a ±3.5 m corridor, a 9 m podium at the male, a 5 m patch per lioness and a 20 m fore-court at the lens; hold pins behaviour so the settle cannot wander the pride off. Both captures use an identical camera (d=8, pitch 10, yaw −87.1°) — the lottery is gone. Draw calls 185 (was 190); waterhole unchanged at 200. Remaining nit: the male's flank reads pale-bright at full front-rake — a lighting tune, not an occlusion defect.

PARTIALLY RESOLVED (2026-09-08): the texture-pattern half of this minor is fixed via terrain's grass rework — the synthetic squiggle stamp at midday (overview through close) is now a soft tufted grain (fix4-game-close-14.png). White sparkle blotches overlap vegetation at the waterhole rim and upper river in overview shots (blind-sav-overview.png) — reads as specular aliasing; needs a real-GPU cross-check before treating as a shader bug.

issues.text: FIXED (2026-09-05, environment/atmosphere.js): the round-1 SYSTEMIC 'everything washes out toward white' blocker was never a tone-mapping or albedo-authoring problem — it was a CPU sky-sampler aliasing bug that made every sky-derived colour ~10^4x too dim, driving the exposure controller to its ceiling and fog/horizon colours to near-black. Full root cause under environment's entry. The earlier 'author darker to compensate' guidance was a workaround over a defect and is wrong.

FIXED (2026-09-05, park module verified): the full game now starts into a complete playable park — park auto-builds on core:ready (gate, lodge complex, loop + spurs, 4 habitats, 60+ animals, 4 tours, sim at speed 1). FIXED (2026-09-08) and real-GPU-verified: white sparkle blotches along waterlines, pan rims and 'fence rings' at overview were genuine specular aliasing (persists on AMD RX 5700 XT D3D11 — not a SwiftShader artifact). Terrain wet-band roughness 0.34→0.50 with a +0.35 roughness floor over 200–800 m, detail normals flattening to 15% past 700 m, and water glint ×0.1 by 800 m. Day speckle gone in game and savannah overviews on real GPU; game-overview draws/tris bit-identical. Night clarification: the dotted rings at 21.5h are pale-sand ALBEDO (byte-identical before/after), pre-existing and unchanged — not part of this bug; residual night road-line sparkle is roads' reflective paint.

World-edge apron reads as a low-detail continuation: the palette was re-matched (2026-09-05, terrain/apron.js) and the bright-slab effect is gone, but the border is still visible as a detail-density step (habitat tints, roads and props exist only inside the world). Acceptable at gameplay distances; a perfect match would mean extending the splat material itself. Re-confirmed by the 2026-09-07 blind overview shots.
